# Freeze store integrity maintenance

Ensure the `TextFileBasedViolationStore` maintains the integrity of its `stored.rules` index and files.

Setting `default.integrity` to `repair` will check the index and folder as they are on disk during initialization, even if the same folder was initialized before. Defaulting to `ignore` which checks nothing.

If an entry points to a path that is not a regular file directly within the folder, it is broken. This also applies if the file name is not a valid path.

If an entry is not broken and its file has no violations it is resolved. Files that only contain line breaks are also resolved.

Entries that point to the same file name are shared, even if nothing exists with that name. If multiple entries point to the same regular file they are also shared. Including through a symbolic or hard link. Even if that file is outside the folder.

The `TextFileBasedViolationStore` will not touch any shared entries or files that no entry points to. If an entry is shared and anything else it will remain shared.

When set to `repair` broken entries will be discarded without touching whatever they point to.

When set to `repair` resolved entries and the file they point to will be discarded. If a resolved entry is a symbolic link the file it points to will be deleted as well.

If using `repair` and saving no violations for a known rule it will forget the rule. Its entry will be removed and its file as well. Unless another entry is sharing that file. In which case only the entry will be removed. Even if it points outside the folder. If using `repair` and saving no violations for an unknown rule nothing will be saved.

If it cannot delete the file of a rule it is forgetting it will fail to save and leave the entry.

### Summary of Changes

The integrity maintenance feature for `TextFileBasedViolationStore` has been implemented according to the specification.

#### 1. Configuration & Integrity Repair on Initialization
- Added support for the configuration property `default.integrity`:
  - Defaults to `ignore` (no integrity checks performed).
  - When set to `repair`, performs index and folder integrity checks during initialization on disk, even if the same folder was initialized previously (via `storedRules.reload()`).
- Added implementation in [`TextFileBasedViolationStore.java`](file:///app/archunit/src/main/java/com/tngtech/archunit/library/freeze/TextFileBasedViolationStore.java):
  - Constants `INTEGRITY_PROPERTY_NAME = "default.integrity"`, `INTEGRITY_DEFAULT = "ignore"`, and `INTEGRITY_REPAIR = "repair"`.
  - Detection of **shared entries**:
    - Entries pointing to the same file name (even if non-existent).
    - Entries pointing to the same regular file (including symbolic links or hard links, even if outside the folder).
    - Shared entries and unreferenced files are never touched.
  - Detection and handling of **broken entries**:
    - An entry is broken if its target is not a regular file directly within the folder (e.g. subdirectories, non-existent files, parent directory traversal, invalid path syntax).
    - Discarded from index without touching whatever they point to.
  - Detection and handling of **resolved entries**:
    - An entry is resolved if it is not broken and its file contains no violations (including files containing only line breaks).
    - Both the entry in `stored.rules` and the file on disk are discarded. If the file is a symbolic link, the symlink and its target file are deleted.
- Extended [`FileSyncedProperties`](file:///app/archunit/src/main/java/com/tngtech/archunit/library/freeze/TextFileBasedViolationStore.java) with thread-safe synchronized methods: `remove(String)`, `removeWithoutSync(String)`, `reload()`, and `getAllProperties()`.

#### 2. Runtime Behavior on `save(...)`
- When `repair` is active and saving 0 violations for an **unknown rule**:
  - Does nothing (saves no entry and creates no file).
- When `repair` is active and saving 0 violations for a **known rule**:
  - Forgets the rule by removing its entry from `stored.rules` and deleting its file (including target file if symlinked, even outside the folder).
  - If the file is shared with another entry, removes only the entry and keeps the file intact.
  - If deleting the file fails (e.g., read-only filesystem or permissions), throws `StoreUpdateFailedException` and leaves the entry in `stored.rules`.

#### 3. Test Coverage
Added comprehensive unit tests in [`TextFileBasedViolationStoreTest.java`](file:///app/archunit/src/test/java/com/tngtech/archunit/library/freeze/TextFileBasedViolationStoreTest.java):
- Default behavior (`default.integrity=ignore`): leaves broken, resolved, and shared entries intact.
- `default.integrity=repair`:
  - Discards broken entries (directories, nested paths, non-existent files, broken symlinks) without modifying the disk targets.
  - Deletes resolved entries and their files (empty files, whitespace/newline-only files, symlinked target files).
  - Preserves shared entries (same file name, symlink/hardlink aliases) and unreferenced files.
  - Repairs disk state upon re-initialization of an already-cached store folder.
  - Handles `save` with 0 violations for unknown rules (saves nothing) and known rules (removes entry, deletes file and symlink target, retains file if shared, and throws exception leaving the entry intact if file deletion fails).

---

### Verification
- Tested specifically with `./gradlew :archunit:test --tests "com.tngtech.archunit.library.freeze.*"`: all freeze tests passed.
- Executed the full project test suite with `./gradlew test`: all 103 Gradle tasks completed successfully with 0 failures.
